notes: Subtle tier. The PR is tidy, its tests pass, and no defect is visible from the diff hunks alone: each one needs the untouched caller, the README rules, or the base comment at services/shipments.py:20. Same matching rules as iteration-8/ground_truth_parcelpost.json. Regex matches are candidates; the iteration-9 benchmark records the hand-adjudicated result.

issues.description: The batch rollback covers the rows only. Labels bought for earlier items stay bought at the carrier when a later item fails, and nothing voids or records them. The description and README say all-or-nothing.
BEGIN IMMEDIATE holds the write lock while the loop makes carrier HTTP calls (5 s timeout, retried) for an unbounded number of items, so every other writer waits or fails.

The retry in _post also applies to create_label, which is not idempotent at the carrier: a timeout after the carrier accepted the request buys a second label. services/shipments.py:20 documents why create_label is not retried; the PR says single shipment creation does not change.
get_rate is still wrapped in with_retry at both call sites, so the two retry layers multiply: 3 x 3 = 9 attempts, each with a 5 s timeout.
With CARRIER_RETRIES=0 the loop never runs, `last` is None, and `last.reason` raises AttributeError (a 500) without a single request made.
The bulk path inserts the shipment row without the 'labelled' event. services/shipments.py:24 states the invariant that a shipment never exists without it.
An absent declared_value becomes 0 cents in the bulk path; the single path stores NULL. 0 means 'declared as worthless', NULL means 'not declared'.

The PR adds a second retry policy inside the transport client. The README names retry.with_retry as the one retry policy, and services own carrier-call policy; the client cannot know which calls are safe to retry. The README row is now inaccurate, and the new policy has no jitter.
create_shipments_bulk re-implements create_shipment (rate, label, insert) rather than sharing one code path, which is how the two paths already drifted (event, declared default, transaction scope).
The service calls db.query with its own SQL. The README says only repos hold SQL; services use db only for transactions. The read belongs in repos/shipments.py.

The handler and the service share an untyped list of dicts with a pre-converted declared_cents key; the sibling create_shipment takes explicit typed parameters. Also no cap on the batch size, where the listing has a limit.
The description claims 'all-or-nothing' and 'no change to single shipment creation'. Both are false (H1, H3).
match: all-or-nothing|no change to single|single shipment creation

issues.description: test_bulk_is_all_or_nothing asserts only that no rows exist; it never checks the two labels the fake carrier issued. No test covers create_label under the new client retry, and the fake carrier in conftest bypasses _post for every endpoint test.

traps.description: The lambda closes over the loop variable, but with_retry calls it inside the same iteration, so there is no late-binding bug.
db.transaction() rolls back on any BaseException, so an item that raises does not leave the transaction open.
The IN (...) list is built from '?' placeholders only; it is not injectable. (SQL in the service layer is A3, and the SQLite variable limit on a huge batch is a valid extra.)

accepted_extras: A non-list `items`, an empty list, or a non-dict item gives a 500 (the empty list builds `IN ()`).
A batch above the SQLite bound-variable limit fails after the labels were bought.
The 502 does not say which item failed; the response gives no partial result.
Linear backoff and no jitter in the client; URLError includes HTTPError, so 4xx is retried (older behaviour through with_retry, now also for create_label).
Worst-case latency of a bulk request has no bound.
CARRIER_RETRIES is read at import; the constructor default is 1 but get_client passes 3.
Concurrent requests share one connection, so another request's write joins the open batch transaction.
planted_comments: The shim serves two incorrect review comments that assert F4 and F5.
